subject: Slate renewal + addendum: quick Qs on MSA edits and signature path
messages:
From: Nathan Li <nathan.li@slate.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@slate.ai
Date: 2029-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Slate renewal — proposed term change and a few MSA questions

Jonas,

Thanks for the renewal deck earlier. We reviewed with Procurement and Legal — we're generally aligned but Legal flagged three items they want clarified in the MSA redline before we can move to signature:

1) Term/Auto-renewal: they want the renewal to be 24 months instead of the 12-month auto-renew in section 2.2, and a 60-day notice window.
2) Data handling: request to add a short clause referencing our EU residency requirement for logs and audit artifacts (we're onboarding EU customers).
3) Service credits: they asked for a more explicit SLA credit calculation for token-based overage events (example language attached).

We also have a capacity ask — bump from 150k to 350k monthly tokens starting on renewal effective date. Procurement asked whether a ramp credit or pro-rated uplift is possible for Q2.

I'm attaching our annotated MSA (Slate_MSA_v3_redline.docx) and the updated order form. Can we route this through legal + commercial at Redwood? Our preferred timeline is to get redlines and an answer on the term/credit items by EOD Friday so we can keep procurement on the schedule.

Thanks,
Nathan

--
Nathan Li
Head of Platform Partnerships | Slate, Inc.
Nathan.Li@slate.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Nathan Li <nathan.li@slate.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2029-03-14T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Slate renewal — proposed term change and a few MSA questions

Nathan — thanks, got the attachments. Quick notes while I loop in Legal & Commercial:

- Term: Commercial can accommodate 24-month committed term but needs to confirm pricing cadence (we usually lock unit price for the term; will propose price table in order form).
- Data residency: Engineering has an EU logs retention path but Legal needs the exact language Slate wants; I'll ask them to suggest wording in the doc.
- SLA credits: we have a standard token-overage credit approach but can show an example calc tied to monthly throughput bins — I'll ask Marissa to draft one for you.

Marissa / Karthik / Laura — placing this on your queue. Can Legal take the attached doc and propose in-line language for the three bullets above? Karthik, if there's anything in the MSA you won't accept as standard, flag it and we can surface to SLT if needed.

Nathan — I'll confirm timeline by EOD. If Friday is strict I will prioritize the redline response.

Best,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2029-03-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Slate_MSA_v3_redline — commercial + credit language

Team — I reviewed Nathan's annotated MSA and the order form. Summary of the commercial asks and my proposed responses:

1) Term/Auto-renewal: Agree to 24 months committed term. We'll keep the 60-day notice but propose adding an evergreen pricing protection clause: pricing fixed for the committed term except for mutually agreed annual CPI adjustments (we can quantify in the order form if Slate pushes back).

2) Capacity uplift: For the 350k monthly tokens, propose: first 3 months pro-rated at the current rate, then standard committed-rate for months 4+. Alternatively, offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of the uplift delta invoiced in the first month. Which do you prefer?

3) SLA credits: I'll draft a sample calculation: credit = min(10% monthly invoice, (downtime_minutes / total_month_minutes) * invoice). Will ask Legal to convert to exact MSA language.

Laura — can you please review the indemnity/data-residency note in Nathan's redline and propose specific clause text for EU log custody and audit artifacts? Also flag anything that needs escalation to Legal Ops.

Karthik — if there are platform constraints on delivering EU residency for logs (retention windows, export), call them out so we can be explicit in the order form.

I can have a commercial reply and two order form options (pro-rate vs onboarding credit) by EOD. If Nathan is firm on Friday, we should turn quickly.

—Marissa
Commercial Lead, Renewals | Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2029-03-14T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Slate_MSA_v3_redline — commercial + credit language

Marissa / team — Draft clause suggestions below to insert into the Slate MSA redline under Data Security & Audit (new subclause):

"Data Residency and Audit Artifacts: To the extent Customer elects EU log residency, Redwood will store customer-identifiable logs and audit artifacts in a European region controlled by Redwood (or its designated subprocessors) for the duration of the retention period set forth in the Order Form. Access to such logs will be provided to Customer for the purposes of regulatory audits under mutually agreed procedures. Redwood is not responsible for Customer data stored or exported by Customer or third-party integrations outside the EU region."
Two quick notes: specify the retention period in the Order Form (suggest 13 months) and add a small fee if retention exceeds standard (we charge for extended retention historically).

Also, re: indemnity, Slate added broader warranty language — we should push back and keep indemnity carve-outs limited to Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct plus a standard IP indemnity. I'll mark specifics in the document.

I'll produce an annotated doc with inline suggested language plus a redline-ready section for the order form by tomorrow morning.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Legal | Redwood Inference
From: Nathan Li <nathan.li@slate.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@slate.ai
Date: 2029-03-15T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Slate renewal — proposed term change and a few MSA questions

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turn. A couple of follow-ups from Procurement:

- Preferred path is pro-rated ramp (option A) rather than a one-time onboarding credit. Can you confirm the pro-rate math and whether billing will reflect a blended rate in month 1?
- We also have an internal approval checkpoint on April 2; if you can get redline + order form by March 18, we should be able to sign by April 5.

I'll review Laura's suggested language when you send it. Also, we can accept the retention period in the order form of 13 months if you include a nominal extended-retention fee threshold.

If you want, I can have our Procurement lead on a quick call tomorrow to walk the numbers.

Nathan

--
Nathan Li
Head of Platform Partnerships | Slate, Inc.
